findings.issue_text: The query to find embed_category returns an empty result set when unconfigured, and calling [0]['id'] on the empty result raises NoMethodError, crashing the migration. The fallback on lines 12-13 is unreachable because the crash happens first.

Host values from embeddable_hosts site setting are interpolated directly into raw SQL INSERT with '#{h}', allowing SQL injection if a host value contains a single quote. Parameterized queries should be used.

update and destroy actions in embeddable_hosts_controller call EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first without checking for nil, causing NoMethodError on nil.host= or nil.destroy when the host doesn't exist.
The update action in embedding_controller ignores all request parameters and simply re-renders the current @embedding object, making the endpoint a no-op where nothing is ever persisted.

The before_validation callback in embeddable_host model calls self.host.sub!(...) without guarding against nil, raising NoMethodError before format validation can report the error gracefully when host is nil.

expandable_first_post? in topic.rb removed the SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? check, so any topic with an embed is expandable when embed_truncate is enabled even if no EmbeddableHost records exist in the database.
type.replace('_', '-') in rest.js.es6 only replaces the first underscore occurrence, causing ADMIN_MODELS lookup to fail for model names with multiple underscores.
Fabricator file contents are swapped: category_fabricator.rb contains the embeddable_host fabricator while embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains all category fabricators.

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The update action in embedding_controller ignores all request parameters and simply re-renders the current @embedding object, making the endpoint a no-op where nothing is ever persisted.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `update` does not read or permit any request params and does not modify/persist anything; it simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` where `@embedding` is an `OpenStruct` created in `fetch_embedding` (id: 'default', embeddable_hosts: EmbeddableHost.all...). Therefore the PUT `/admin/customize/embedding` endpoint is effectively a no-op and cannot persist changes to any embedding-level settings via this controller.

adjudication_records.issue_text: expandable_first_post? in topic.rb removed the SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? check, so any topic with an embed is expandable when embed_truncate is enabled even if no EmbeddableHost records exist in the database.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` from `Topic#expandable_first_post?`, so the method now depends only on `SiteSetting.embed_truncate?` and `has_topic_embed?`. However, `embeddable_hosts` as a site setting is removed in this change and embedding authorization is now driven by `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` (used in `EmbedController` and `TopicRetriever`). If there are no `EmbeddableHost` records, new embedded topics won’t be created, so in normal operation there won’t be topics where `has_topic_embed?` is true. And even if legacy embedded topics exist, making them expandable when `embed_truncate` is enabled is not clearly a defect—`embed_truncate` is the explicit switch controlling that behavior. The finding describes a behavioral change but not a clear, verifiable bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: type.replace('_', '-') in rest.js.es6 only replaces the first underscore occurrence, causing ADMIN_MODELS lookup to fail for model names with multiple underscores.

adjudication.rationale: In `rest.js.es6`, `basePath(store, type)` now checks `ADMIN_MODELS.indexOf(type.replace('_', '-'))`. It is true that `String#replace('_','-')` only replaces the first underscore, but in this diff `ADMIN_MODELS` contains only entries that correspond to types with at most one underscore (e.g. `site_customization` -> `site-customization`, `embeddable_host` -> `embeddable-host`). There is no model name with multiple underscores added/used here, so no lookup failure is verifiably introduced by this change in the provided diff. The finding relies on hypothetical future model names, which is speculative.
